article.headline: Nylander ties a career high with 5 points, Maple Leafs beat Avs, 6-3
article.description: — William Nylander and Easton Cowan scored 46 seconds apart late in the second period and the Toronto Maple Leafs beat the Colorado Avalanche 6-3 on Saturday night.

article.story: DENVER -- — William Nylander and Easton Cowan scored 46 seconds apart late in the second period and the Toronto Maple Leafs beat the Colorado Avalanche 6-3 on Saturday night. Nylander finished with two goals and had a career-high three assists to finish with five points, also tying a career high. Auston Matthews had two goals and two assists for Toronto, which has alternated wins and losses to start the season. Nathan MacKinnon scored twice for Colorado, which suffered its first loss in three home games. Brock Nelson also scored and Mackenzie Blackwood had 16 saves in his first setback of the season. The Avs finished 0 of 5 on the power play, which included eight seconds of a 5 on 3 early in the second period. After Nick Blankenburg gave the Maple Leafs a 1-0 lead 3:03 into the game, MacKinnon’s bull-rush through the Toronto defense tied it midway through the first. He gave Colorado the lead with his second of the night at 15:14. Nylander tied it 19 seconds after Jaden Schwartz took high-sticking minor early in the second, the first power-play goal the Avs allowed this season. Brock Nelson scored off his own rebound later in the period to give Colorado a 3-2 lead before the Maple Leafs grabbed control in the second. Nylander’s second of the night tied it at 16:47 and Cowan scored a one-timer off a pass from Morgan Reilly gave Toronto the lead at 17:33. The Matthews made it 5-3 with a power-play goal midway through the third and sealed it when he scored into an empty net in the final minute. Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 30 shots. Avalanche forward Logan O’Connor was away from the team following the sudden passing of his father, former NHL defenseman Myles O’Connor. Up next Maple Leafs: Wrap up their three-game trip at Utah on Tuesday night. Avalanche: At Dallas on Tuesday night. ------ AP NHL: https://apnews.com/hub/nhl
